resources.string: Google permissions determine which API actions are available. App tool policies below separately control Ask, Allow and Deny. Opening this screen never grants permissions.
Deny on a Google permission disconnects both Gmail and Drive locally. To block only one action, use its tool policy below.

gmail.modify permits reading, drafting and sending at Google, as well as labels, archive, read state, spam, trash and restore. It cannot permanently delete messages. These Google permissions do not authorize autonomous app actions.

Full mail access includes reading, drafting, sending, mailbox management and permanent message deletion. Enable it only if needed. Each irreversible action requires review of the exact targets; it cannot use Allow. Deleting a label also permanently removes its label assignments and requires review.

This send-only Google token cannot verify its account. Sending is unavailable until you explicitly enable a profile-capable permission, such as drafts, or reconnect with Android authorization. No extra permission is requested automatically.
Google permissions belong to different accounts or the account changed. No action was sent. Reconnect the intended account and review the action again.
Google did not return a verifiable Gmail account. No action was sent.
The verified Google account could not be saved. No action was sent.

gmail.labels permits creating, reading, renaming and deleting label definitions. It does not read mail or apply labels to messages; message organization needs Manage mail. Deleting a label permanently removes its assignments and requires review for every action.

This labels-only Google token cannot verify its account. Label edits are unavailable until you explicitly enable a profile-capable management permission or reconnect with Android authorization. No extra permission is requested automatically.
